I read SKILL.md (249 lines) and references/dx-calibration.md (185 lines) in full and grepped the directory for commit|read.only|no changes|non-destructive|do not (change|modify|edit|write)|only read|without changing|leave.*unchanged. The skill leans advisory at SKILL.md:239-242 ("recommend"), but nowhere declares itself read-only or forbids commits, and SKILL.md:208's Step 9 method ("fix the biggest bottleneck first → iterate") actively reads as license to modify the repo — while the skill is simultaneously instructed to run builds and CLI commands, which mutate the tree. Gap is real: the KICKOFF sentence is the only restraint and must be KEPT; the skill should carry an explicit read-only declaration.

verdicts.evidence: SKILL.md:18-19 — "**Division of labor:** this is the milestone-level reality check, not a per-phase pass — run it / once the product's getting-started surface is actually stable, not mid-milestone." (verified; the quoted clause spans L18 into L19, the claim cited L18 only)
verdicts.reasoning: REFUTED. The skill states a precondition ("run it once the getting-started surface is actually stable") but has no way to evaluate it — it cannot know where in the milestone it sits or whether the surface has settled. The operator's two-word qualifier "now-stable" (KICKOFF L1016-1017, verified) asserts that the skill's own precondition is satisfied at this point in the pipeline; that is the operator supplying a state judgement the skill demands and cannot make, which the rubric classes as conditional gating the operator must judge, not restatement. It is also incidental phrasing inside a sentence whose actual job is "have it walk that real flow" — it duplicates none of the skill's methodology (the nine audit steps), gates, or scorecard template. Reclassified load-bearing-parameter, low.

The enumeration maps one-to-one onto three of the skill's nine mandatory audit steps: "time-to-hello-world" = Step 1's TTHW tier output (L124-136), "CLI --help output" = Step 2's literal instruction "run `--help`" (L140), "the errors a newcomer actually hits" = Step 3 Error Message Audit (L145-161). verdicts.reasoning: KICKOFF L1018-1019 verified: "This is a gate: tell me plainly whether it passed, because a failing scorecard blocks the ship." I read SKILL.md and references/dx-calibration.md end to end and grepped the directory for gate|pass|fail|block|verdict|threshold|bar|approve|reject|ship. Every hit is unrelated: "if devs write their own HTTP wrapper, you failed" (SKILL.md:69, a cognitive pattern), "not a per-phase pass" (L18), "pass the wrong ID type" (dx-calibration.md:37), "docs ship with the feature" (dx-calibration.md:114), "ship several times faster" (dx-calibration.md:154). The TTHW table (L88-95) grades tiers by adoption impact, not pass/fail. Nowhere does the skill declare a passing threshold, emit a PASS/FAIL verdict, or state that a low score blocks anything; "Next Steps" (L237-242) only recommends fixes and a re-run. The KICKOFF sentence is therefore the sole thing converting a scorecard into a ship gate — load-bearing, must be KEPT. High severity: without it the step-12 milestone gate degrades silently into an advisory report. Note the identical sentence carries the accessibility-tester block at KICKOFF:1008-1009, so this looks like a repeated pattern of the guide supplying gate semantics the gate skills lack.
